**Continuous 2.38.7**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.38.6, 2.38.5, 2.38.4, 2.38.3, 2.38.2, 2.38.1, 2.38.0, 2.36.0, 2.34.0, 2.32.0, 2.30.0, 2.28.0, 2.26.0, 2.24.0, 2.22.0, 2.20.0, 2.18.0, 2.16.3, 2.16.2, 2.16.1, 2.16.0, 2.14.0, 2.12.x, 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.38.7.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.38.7.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.38.7.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.38.7.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.38.7.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.38.7.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.38.7.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.38.7-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.38.7.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.38.7-vscode/continuous-cli-2.38.7.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). The short command `cn` also works; both run the same program. It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.38.6

This release is about the chat in a narrow sidebar, clearer errors, and small local models. At the default sidebar width the model name no longer disappears under the prompt. A message that cannot be drawn no longer offers to throw the conversation away. Ollama keeps its tools after a tool result, and uses the context window the server loaded. On Windows, stopping a command also stops what it started.

No new host is contacted by the extension or the terminal agent. An Ollama server you already use gets two more requests the first time a model with no context length set is used.

### New

- **Small context windows.** When the tools and instructions take more than half of a model's room for input, one line above the prompt gives the numbers and offers Chat mode or the short prompt.
- **Window in use.** For a local model, the model list shows the context window the server reported, for example "(4,096 tokens, from the server)".
- **No model selected.** Sending with no chat model says so and offers "Add a model". Your message stays in the box.
- **Keyboard focus.** The control that has keyboard focus shows an outline in the theme's focus colour. The links in error notices, the History clear-search icon and the tool-call rows that open something are buttons you can reach with Tab.
- **Terminal agent: why it asks.** The approval prompt says why the call asks and where that was decided: your rule and its file, or the built-in check. `r` shows the full reason and the narrowest rule that would allow the call.

### Behaviour changes

- **Ollama context length.** With no context length set here or in the Modelfile, Continuous no longer sends `num_ctx`. It loads the model, reads the window the server gave it and cuts the prompt to that. On a small GPU that can be 4,096 tokens, less than the 8,192 that was forced before. Set a context length on the model to choose your own.
- **Loop checks in the editor.** An item's check now runs where a terminal command runs: PowerShell by default on Windows (it was `cmd.exe`), or WSL or a container when `terminal.shell` says so. Checks are linted like terminal commands, are stopped with everything they started when their time is up, and no longer receive secret-named environment variables unless `terminal.passEnv` names them. A check written for `cmd.exe` may need changing.
- **Tool arguments.** A string sent where a tool expects a list, a number or true/false is read as that value, on every call. A parameter that may be a string is never changed.
- **Terminal agent: failed commands.** A failed command's result starts with its exit code, and includes what it printed as well as its errors. A command that failed with nothing on stderr used to look like a success.
- **Terminal agent: unreadable arguments.** A tool call whose arguments could not be read is answered and not run. It used to run with no arguments.
- **`.prompt` files.** The grammar scope is `source.continuous-prompt`, so it no longer collides with the original extension. A theme or setting that names `source.prompt` no longer applies to these files here.
- **Toolbar under the prompt.** In a narrow sidebar the usage figures move to a second line when the model name would otherwise be squeezed out.

### Fixes

- **Model name.** With usage shown under the prompt, the model name was squeezed to nothing at sidebar widths around 300 pixels. It keeps its place now.
- **Setup form.** The model setup form was still a little wider than its container, which cut off the Review button and the field edges in the dialog ([#982](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/issues/982)). It fits.
- **Reply actions.** The row of buttons under a reply wraps instead of running off the side, and "Compact conversation" shows its label only where it fits.
- **Message that cannot be drawn.** It shows one line with "Show as plain text" and "Copy details". The old "Restart" button started a new conversation.
- **Local server errors.** A connection that fails says which server, host and port, and what to check. It used to say "fetch failed", or give Ollama advice only for one address.
- **Ollama tools.** The tool list was sent only when the last message was yours, so the model had no tools after a tool result. It is sent on every request.
- **`localhost`.** A server that listens only on `::1`, or only on `127.0.0.1`, is reached through `localhost`. The address was rewritten to `127.0.0.1` before.
- **Windows paths in config.** `C:\a\b.yaml` and `\\server\share\b.yaml` are read as files, not as package names.
- **Stopping a command on Windows.** A command that timed out or was stopped left the programs it had started running. They are ended too.
- **Open and closed sections.** Tool details, terminal output, thinking and code blocks keep the state you left them in when you scroll away and back.
- **Compaction estimate.** It was worked out twice for every piece of a streaming reply. It is worked out only while its notice shows.
- **`create_new_file`.** Contents sent as an object are written as indented JSON.
- **Terminal agent: streamed calls.** A tool call streamed without an id was dropped. It runs.
- **Start-up log.** Two optional start-up steps log one line that begins with "Continuous:" when they are skipped, so they can be told apart from the original extension's lines.
